claims.text: Atmospheric plasma spraying can apply an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating to Q235 steel.
Furnace annealing of the coated Q235 steel will produce a continuous passivation layer.
The annealing-induced passivation layer will be located at the AlCoCrFeNi-coating/Q235-steel interface.
The interfacial passivation layer may be an intermetallic or oxide phase.
During annealing, the AlCoCrFeNi coating reacts with ambient oxygen and intrinsic species to form the protective layer.
The passivation layer impedes the ingress and diffusion of corrosive ions or species.
Impeded transport of corrosive species delays corrosion initiation.
The passivation layer prevents or suppresses corrosion propagation.
Coated and annealed Q235 steel will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than untreated Q235 steel under identical corrosive exposure.
Coated and annealed Q235 steel will show a delayed onset of degradation relative to untreated Q235 steel.
The protective effect will operate in harsh corrosive environments at room temperature.
The protective effect will also operate at moderately elevated temperatures around 100°C.
Protection is limited to temperature and corrosive-agent concentration ranges in which the passivation layer remains stable.
Extreme temperatures or highly aggressive corrosive environments may cause the protective layer to break down or form nonuniformly.
Similar coating behavior has previously been observed in systems such as SS316L.
Coating chemistry, microstructural evolution, adhesion, thickness effects, and long-term stability may differ on Q235 steel.
